items.claim: A business-logic data-validation flaw is proved by replaying the same request with identifiers that put the referenced record in a state the workflow forbids (for example an ID belonging to a deceased person when only living ones are valid) and observing the application accept it anyway.
items.body:
A business-logic data-validation flaw is proved by replaying the same request with identifiers that put the referenced record in a state the workflow forbids (for example an ID belonging to a deceased person when only living ones are valid) and observing the application accept it anyway.

HackTricks reference: 9b25d126 (notion:9b25d126-9f9a-41b3-8d70-26d626ceb115)
items.disproof: Every out-of-state or out-of-workflow input is rejected with an error, showing the underlying record state is actually validated rather than assumed.
